# spi_p2s Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

This module converts a parallel 8-bit data byte into a serial bit stream for SPI transmission. It supports three output widths:

- **Single**: one data line, one bit per beat.
- **Dual**: two data lines, two bits per beat.
- **Quad**: four data lines, four bits per beat.

The module also provides an early “byte consumed” indication so the next byte can be requested before the current byte has completely finished shifting out. It does not interpret SPI commands, addresses, or protocols; it only serializes bytes and controls the output drivers for the SPI data lines.

## 2. Behavioral Description

### 2.1 Reset Behavior

On reset:

- The module shall enter its idle/initial state.
- The bit-group counter shall be cleared to the first beat of a byte.
- All SPI output drivers shall be disabled.
- No byte-consumed indication shall be asserted.
- The configured IO mode after reset shall be Single.

### 2.2 Chip-Select and Output Driving

The module shall only drive the SPI data lines when both of the following conditions are true:

- Chip-select is active, meaning asserted low.
- A byte is currently being presented for transmission.

If chip-select is inactive, all SPI output drivers shall be disabled, regardless of whether a byte is being presented.

The data lines that are driven shall depend on the selected IO mode:

- **Single**: one data line is driven.
- **Dual**: two data lines are driven.
- **Quad**: all four data lines are driven.
- **Unsupported mode**: no data lines are driven.

The output data is only meaningful while the corresponding output driver is enabled.

### 2.3 Byte Serialization

A “beat” is one clock-wide transmission unit:

- Single mode: one beat transmits one bit.
- Dual mode: one beat transmits two bits.
- Quad mode: one beat transmits four bits.

On the first beat of a byte, the module shall present the first group of bits directly from the input byte. On each subsequent clock edge, the module shall advance to the next group of bits. After the final group of the byte has been presented, the bit counter shall return to the first beat.

The module shall advance from one beat to the next on the rising edge of the SPI clock, while a byte is being transmitted.

### 2.4 Bit Order

The module shall support two bit-order configurations:

- **MSB-first**: the most significant bit or bit-group is transmitted first.
- **LSB-first**: the least significant bit or bit-group is transmitted first.

The resulting order for a byte is:

| Mode | MSB-first | LSB-first |
|---|---|---|
| Single | bit 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0 | bit 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 |
| Dual | bits [7:6], [5:4], [3:2], [1:0] | bits [1:0], [3:2], [5:4], [7:6] |
| Quad | bits [7:4], [3:0] | bits [3:0], [7:4] |

The selected bit order shall be applied consistently for every byte transmitted.

### 2.5 Byte-Valid Behavior

The byte-valid input indicates that the current input byte is available for transmission.

When byte-valid is asserted and chip-select is active, the module shall drive the selected SPI data lines with the serialized bit groups.

When byte-valid is deasserted, the module shall not drive any SPI data lines.

For proper operation, byte-valid shall remain asserted for the entire duration of a byte transfer. If byte-valid is dropped before the final beat, the transfer is not guaranteed to complete correctly.

### 2.6 Byte-Consumed Indication

The module shall assert a byte-consumed indication one beat before the final beat of the current byte. This early assertion gives the data source enough time to provide the next byte.

For each mode, the indication shall be asserted during:

| Mode | Beat position |
|---|---|
| Single | the seventh one-bit beat of the byte |
| Dual | the third two-bit beat of the byte |
| Quad | the first four-bit beat of the byte |

The indication shall correspond to the currently selected IO mode. In an unsupported mode, the byte-consumed indication shall not be asserted.

### 2.7 Clock-Phase Behavior

The module supports a clock-phase configuration.

- When clock-phase is **0**, the bit counter advances on every active clock edge while a byte is being transmitted.
- When clock-phase is **1**, the first beat after reset is held for one extra clock edge before the module advances to the next beat. This delay applies only to the first byte after reset; subsequent bytes advance normally.

This behavior allows the first bit group to remain stable for the required time in SPI mode 3.

## 3. Configuration Constraints

The following conditions shall be met for correct module operation:

- After reset, the IO mode shall be Single.
- The IO mode may be changed only while the bit counter is at the first beat of a byte.
- The IO mode shall remain stable for the duration of a byte transfer.
- Byte-valid shall not be asserted while chip-select is inactive.
- Chip-select shall remain active for the full byte transfer.

## 4. Summary of Observable Behavior

- The module serializes one byte into one, two, or four parallel SPI output lanes depending on the configured mode.
- It supports both MSB-first and LSB-first ordering.
- It drives outputs only when chip-select is active and byte-valid is asserted.
- It asserts a byte-consumed signal one beat before the last beat of each byte.
- It provides a one-time first-beat delay when clock-phase is 1.
- It resets into a state where no lines are driven and the IO mode must be Single.
